## Mishima: presentation of the new album concert at Poble Espanyol!
One pandemic and many, many, many concerts later, **Mishima** presents their**new album, _L’aigua clara_**(TRIS 2022).
Recorded at Black Box, Peter Deimel’s sanctuary in Angers (France), it not only insists on its commitment to **sonic forcefulness**and **literary depth,** but also sublimates it. Five years after _Ara i res_ (2017), David Carabén (vocals and guitar), Marc Lloret (keyboards), Dani Vega (guitar), Xavi Caparrós (bass) and Alfons Serra (drums) reach the fullness in their**ninth studio album,** the tenth of their career if we add the live _Ara i aquí_ (2019). Maturity was (is) exactly that.
**Mishima** will present their new album next**May 27** at the **Poble Espanyol** in **Barcelona**. Come and meet again with a key band of Catalan music.

Mishima is a seminal Catalan indie pop band that emerged from Barcelona in 1999, carving out a distinct niche with their blend of poetic lyricism and melodic nuance. The group’s lineup features David Carabén on vocals and guitar, Marc Lloret on keyboards, Dani Vega on guitars, alongside Xavi Caparrós on bass and Alfons Serra on drums, the latter two having joined in 2010. Mishima’s early albums—"Lipstick Traces" (2000), "The Fall of Public Man" (2003), and "Trucar a casa, recollir les fotos, pagar la multa" (2005)—laid the groundwork for their introspective songwriting, heavily shaped by Carabén’s evocative narratives.
A pivotal collaboration with producer Paco Loco influenced key records such as "Set tota la vida" (2007), "Ordre i aventura" (2010), and "L’amor feliç" (2012), helping the band refine their sound. In pursuit of fresh creative perspectives, Mishima recorded "L’ansia que cura" (2014) and "Ara i res" (2017) in western France at Studio Black Box with producer Peter Deimel. Celebrating 20 years together, the band released "Ara i aquí" (2019), a milestone album reflecting on their enduring journey. Their most recent release, "L’aigua clara" (2022), begins with the track "El gran lladre", capturing themes of love, life, and existential reflection with vibrant energy.
Throughout their career, Mishima has remained a cornerstone of the Catalan indie scene, continuously evolving while maintaining a signature blend of intimate storytelling and sophisticated indie pop sounds that resonate with audiences both regionally and beyond.

## Biography
Drawing their name from the provocative Japanese author, the intellectually inclined Barcelona indie pop group Mishima assembled near the end of the 1990s. Core participants at the outset comprised lead singer and principal songwriter David Carabén together with Christian Aloy on guitars, Marc Lloret on keyboards, Óscar d'Aniello handling drum programming, and Dani Acedo on bass. The band's opening two albums, Lipstick Traces in 2000 and The Fall of the Public Man in 2003, appeared in English, yet critical and popular recognition arrived only after the switch to Catalan on the third release, Trucar a Casa. Recollir les Fotos. Pagar la Multa from 2005, an approach retained across every subsequent project. Personnel shifts followed, with Dani Vega, Alfons Serra, and Xavi Caparrós taking the places of Aloy, Acedo, and d'Aniello.

Mishima is a seminal Catalan indie pop band that emerged from Barcelona in 1999, carving out a distinct niche with their blend of poetic lyricism and melodic nuance. The group’s lineup features David Carabén on vocals and guitar, Marc Lloret on keyboards, Dani Vega on guitars, alongside Xavi Caparrós on bass and Alfons Serra on drums, the latter two having joined in 2010. Mishima’s early albums—"Lipstick Traces" (2000), "The Fall of Public Man" (2003), and "Trucar a casa, recollir les fotos, pagar la multa" (2005)—laid the groundwork for their introspective songwriting, heavily shaped by Carabén’s evocative narratives.
A pivotal collaboration with producer Paco Loco influenced key records such as "Set tota la vida" (2007), "Ordre i aventura" (2010), and "L’amor feliç" (2012), helping the band refine their sound. In pursuit of fresh creative perspectives, Mishima recorded "L’ansia que cura" (2014) and "Ara i res" (2017) in western France at Studio Black Box with producer Peter Deimel. Celebrating 20 years together, the band released "Ara i aquí" (2019), a milestone album reflecting on their enduring journey. Their most recent release, "L’aigua clara" (2022), begins with the track "El gran lladre", capturing themes of love, life, and existential reflection with vibrant energy.
Throughout their career, Mishima has remained a cornerstone of the Catalan indie scene, continuously evolving while maintaining a signature blend of intimate storytelling and sophisticated indie pop sounds that resonate with audiences both regionally and beyond.

## Biography
Drawing their name from the provocative Japanese author, the intellectually inclined Barcelona indie pop group Mishima assembled near the end of the 1990s. Core participants at the outset comprised lead singer and principal songwriter David Carabén together with Christian Aloy on guitars, Marc Lloret on keyboards, Óscar d'Aniello handling drum programming, and Dani Acedo on bass. The band's opening two albums, Lipstick Traces in 2000 and The Fall of the Public Man in 2003, appeared in English, yet critical and popular recognition arrived only after the switch to Catalan on the third release, Trucar a Casa. Recollir les Fotos. Pagar la Multa from 2005, an approach retained across every subsequent project. Personnel shifts followed, with Dani Vega, Alfons Serra, and Xavi Caparrós taking the places of Aloy, Acedo, and d'Aniello.

## Biography
Drawing their name from the provocative Japanese author, the intellectually inclined Barcelona indie pop group Mishima assembled near the end of the 1990s. Core participants at the outset comprised lead singer and principal songwriter David Carabén together with Christian Aloy on guitars, Marc Lloret on keyboards, Óscar d'Aniello handling drum programming, and Dani Acedo on bass. The band's opening two albums, Lipstick Traces in 2000 and The Fall of the Public Man in 2003, appeared in English, yet critical and popular recognition arrived only after the switch to Catalan on the third release, Trucar a Casa. Recollir les Fotos. Pagar la Multa from 2005, an approach retained across every subsequent project. Personnel shifts followed, with Dani Vega, Alfons Serra, and Xavi Caparrós taking the places of Aloy, Acedo, and d'Aniello.

# Mishima / Joan Miquel Oliver
#### Two of the most outstanding musical projects on the Catalan independent music scene share the stage on an exceptional night when they will perform numbers from their latest albums.
Those who doubt the ability and the talent of Catalan artists to make a name for themselves everywhere ought to take a look at the finest moments of Mishima, the band led by David Carabén which has played more than once at such major festivals as Primavera Sound, but also in Berlin, New York and many more cities where audiences have passionately applauded their set. Here they show once again why they have become a legend of Catalan indie music, playing the songs from their latest disc, _Ara i res_, an improved, distilled version of Mishima. Their eighth disc, recorded once more with Peter Deimel at the Black Box Studio in Angers (France), is at once more sentimental and cynical than previous offerings, more literary, but simpler and brighter as well. At times, however, it can be dark and gloomy too.
Opening the show, however, will be _Atlantis_, the new disc by Joan Miquel Oliver. The Majorcan musician, who was the heart and soul of the defunct Antònia Font, broadens his range of musical styles, incorporating rhythms ranging from anti-folk to electro and from rumba to funk, via pop. The result is songs with lyrics of high literary quality that talk about people: individuals and how they relate to the society they live in, children, lost civilizations and so many men and women who, like us, are seen to be amazed by their own existence.

# La Mercè 2017: Mishima + Joan Miquel Oliver + Sopa de Cabra
### Time Out says
Time Out in partnership wtihGastronosfera
This is the second night that sees popular Catalan bands take to Estrella Damm's Escenari Mediterràniament stage on Bogatell beach. Don't forget that the concerts are free, but space is limited so make sure you get there early to ensure you don't miss the chance to party on the beach while listening to great music.
**7pm. Joan Miquel Oliver**Joan Miquel Oliver, founder, composer and guitarist of the now defunct Mallorcan group Antònia Font, presents his latest solo album, _Atlantis_(2017). It features anti-folk, electro, rumba, funk and pure pop, as well as numerous other influences.
**9pm.Mishima.**
This iconic Barcelona band, created by David Carabén, perform their eighth disc, 'Ara i res' (2017); the title comes from a poem by Joan Vinyoli. The album was released following a longer break than is usual with the group, which has previously tended to head to the studio every two years, and was produced by Peter Deimel (a regular partner) in the Black Box Studio in Angers (France).
**11pm. Sopa de Cabra**
Sopa de Cabra, one of the most emblematic Catalan pop groups from the 1990s, come together once more to give a performance that will mean a lot to their numerous fans.
**1am.****Rumberos Pugin a l'Escenari**Catalan rumba is a key musical force in Barcelona and this show will feature renowned names from the scene such as Los Amaya, Rumba Tres, Gertrudis and La Pegatina, among many others. It promises to be a fabulous end to a great night full of music.

## Biography
There are multiple bands called Mishima:
1) Saying the name Mishima is speaking about not only the great Japanese writer but one of Barcelona’s most influential bands of the 21st Century. Despite the fact they started singing in English, the five-piece band fronted by David Carabén started using his mother tongue around 2005 and paved the way for the new wave of indie bands writing songs in Catalan language. Loved by the press and with a fan base growing in geometrical progression, they’ve just released a new album, their seventh, recorded at the mythical Black Box Studios with the help of Peter Deimel (The Kills, The Last Shadow Puppets, Anna Calvi). Hailed as their best, “L’ànsia que cura” (TRIS-Warner, 2014), captures the raw energy of their live set and a sophisticated range of influences including The Smiths and JG. Ballard, Randy Newman and David Lynch, Tindersticks and the chanson française. Think The National born and raised by the Mediterranean Sea.

# Mishima / Joan Miquel Oliver
#### Two of the most outstanding musical projects on the Catalan independent music scene share the stage on an exceptional night when they will perform numbers from their latest albums.
Those who doubt the ability and the talent of Catalan artists to make a name for themselves everywhere ought to take a look at the finest moments of Mishima, the band led by David Carabén which has played more than once at such major festivals as Primavera Sound, but also in Berlin, New York and many more cities where audiences have passionately applauded their set. Here they show once again why they have become a legend of Catalan indie music, playing the songs from their latest disc, _Ara i res_, an improved, distilled version of Mishima. Their eighth disc, recorded once more with Peter Deimel at the Black Box Studio in Angers (France), is at once more sentimental and cynical than previous offerings, more literary, but simpler and brighter as well. At times, however, it can be dark and gloomy too.
Opening the show, however, will be _Atlantis_, the new disc by Joan Miquel Oliver. The Majorcan musician, who was the heart and soul of the defunct Antònia Font, broadens his range of musical styles, incorporating rhythms ranging from anti-folk to electro and from rumba to funk, via pop. The result is songs with lyrics of high literary quality that talk about people: individuals and how they relate to the society they live in, children, lost civilizations and so many men and women who, like us, are seen to be amazed by their own existence.

# La Mercè 2017: Mishima + Joan Miquel Oliver + Sopa de Cabra
### Time Out says
Time Out in partnership wtihGastronosfera
This is the second night that sees popular Catalan bands take to Estrella Damm's Escenari Mediterràniament stage on Bogatell beach. Don't forget that the concerts are free, but space is limited so make sure you get there early to ensure you don't miss the chance to party on the beach while listening to great music.
**7pm. Joan Miquel Oliver**Joan Miquel Oliver, founder, composer and guitarist of the now defunct Mallorcan group Antònia Font, presents his latest solo album, _Atlantis_(2017). It features anti-folk, electro, rumba, funk and pure pop, as well as numerous other influences.
**9pm.Mishima.**
This iconic Barcelona band, created by David Carabén, perform their eighth disc, 'Ara i res' (2017); the title comes from a poem by Joan Vinyoli. The album was released following a longer break than is usual with the group, which has previously tended to head to the studio every two years, and was produced by Peter Deimel (a regular partner) in the Black Box Studio in Angers (France).
**11pm. Sopa de Cabra**
Sopa de Cabra, one of the most emblematic Catalan pop groups from the 1990s, come together once more to give a performance that will mean a lot to their numerous fans.
**1am.****Rumberos Pugin a l'Escenari**Catalan rumba is a key musical force in Barcelona and this show will feature renowned names from the scene such as Los Amaya, Rumba Tres, Gertrudis and La Pegatina, among many others. It promises to be a fabulous end to a great night full of music.

## Biography
There are multiple bands called Mishima:
1) Saying the name Mishima is speaking about not only the great Japanese writer but one of Barcelona’s most influential bands of the 21st Century. Despite the fact they started singing in English, the five-piece band fronted by David Carabén started using his mother tongue around 2005 and paved the way for the new wave of indie bands writing songs in Catalan language. Loved by the press and with a fan base growing in geometrical progression, they’ve just released a new album, their seventh, recorded at the mythical Black Box Studios with the help of Peter Deimel (The Kills, The Last Shadow Puppets, Anna Calvi). Hailed as their best, “L’ànsia que cura” (TRIS-Warner, 2014), captures the raw energy of their live set and a sophisticated range of influences including The Smiths and JG. Ballard, Randy Newman and David Lynch, Tindersticks and the chanson française. Think The National born and raised by the Mediterranean Sea.

# Mishima / Joan Miquel Oliver
#### Two of the most outstanding musical projects on the Catalan independent music scene share the stage on an exceptional night when they will perform numbers from their latest albums.
Those who doubt the ability and the talent of Catalan artists to make a name for themselves everywhere ought to take a look at the finest moments of Mishima, the band led by David Carabén which has played more than once at such major festivals as Primavera Sound, but also in Berlin, New York and many more cities where audiences have passionately applauded their set. Here they show once again why they have become a legend of Catalan indie music, playing the songs from their latest disc, _Ara i res_, an improved, distilled version of Mishima. Their eighth disc, recorded once more with Peter Deimel at the Black Box Studio in Angers (France), is at once more sentimental and cynical than previous offerings, more literary, but simpler and brighter as well. At times, however, it can be dark and gloomy too.
Opening the show, however, will be _Atlantis_, the new disc by Joan Miquel Oliver. The Majorcan musician, who was the heart and soul of the defunct Antònia Font, broadens his range of musical styles, incorporating rhythms ranging from anti-folk to electro and from rumba to funk, via pop. The result is songs with lyrics of high literary quality that talk about people: individuals and how they relate to the society they live in, children, lost civilizations and so many men and women who, like us, are seen to be amazed by their own existence.

### Time Out says
Time Out in partnership wtihGastronosfera
This is the second night that sees popular Catalan bands take to Estrella Damm's Escenari Mediterràniament stage on Bogatell beach. Don't forget that the concerts are free, but space is limited so make sure you get there early to ensure you don't miss the chance to party on the beach while listening to great music.
**7pm. Joan Miquel Oliver**Joan Miquel Oliver, founder, composer and guitarist of the now defunct Mallorcan group Antònia Font, presents his latest solo album, _Atlantis_(2017). It features anti-folk, electro, rumba, funk and pure pop, as well as numerous other influences.
**9pm.Mishima.**
This iconic Barcelona band, created by David Carabén, perform their eighth disc, 'Ara i res' (2017); the title comes from a poem by Joan Vinyoli. The album was released following a longer break than is usual with the group, which has previously tended to head to the studio every two years, and was produced by Peter Deimel (a regular partner) in the Black Box Studio in Angers (France).
**11pm. Sopa de Cabra**
Sopa de Cabra, one of the most emblematic Catalan pop groups from the 1990s, come together once more to give a performance that will mean a lot to their numerous fans.
**1am.****Rumberos Pugin a l'Escenari**Catalan rumba is a key musical force in Barcelona and this show will feature renowned names from the scene such as Los Amaya, Rumba Tres, Gertrudis and La Pegatina, among many others. It promises to be a fabulous end to a great night full of music.

## Biography
There are multiple bands called Mishima:
1) Saying the name Mishima is speaking about not only the great Japanese writer but one of Barcelona’s most influential bands of the 21st Century. Despite the fact they started singing in English, the five-piece band fronted by David Carabén started using his mother tongue around 2005 and paved the way for the new wave of indie bands writing songs in Catalan language. Loved by the press and with a fan base growing in geometrical progression, they’ve just released a new album, their seventh, recorded at the mythical Black Box Studios with the help of Peter Deimel (The Kills, The Last Shadow Puppets, Anna Calvi). Hailed as their best, “L’ànsia que cura” (TRIS-Warner, 2014), captures the raw energy of their live set and a sophisticated range of influences including The Smiths and JG. Ballard, Randy Newman and David Lynch, Tindersticks and the chanson française. Think The National born and raised by the Mediterranean Sea.
